item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00398","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C05","C16","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C05","confidence":0.87,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C05 plausibly supplied a material argumentative template for the child: describe a veterans' benefit proposal, acknowledge the legitimate goal, contrast the proposal with an existing comprehensive program, object that a benefit limited to a selected class would create serious inequities or discrimination among similarly situated veterans, and identify a broader, more equitable mechanism for providing assistance. C16 and C04 use related equality and selective-benefit objections, but C05 provides the closest combination of veterans policy, program expansion, discrimination analysis, and an alternative general system.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"These funds are to be made available only to a limited number of veterans... I cannot approve a program that has such a potential inflationary effect upon the economy or that is so discriminatory. There is no justifiable reason for making loans... available to some veterans and denying them to others.","parent_excerpt":"The practice of making gifts of special non-monetary benefits, such as automobiles, to a particular group of disabled veterans, leads both to serious inequity and to abuse... This bill would create wholesale inequities.","explanation":"Both reject legislation that singles out a limited category of veterans for a special material benefit while excluding other veterans with comparable claims."},{"child_excerpt":"Help to veterans in the field of housing can be met most effectively with programs available to all our citizens, veterans and non-veterans alike, through the coordinated activities of the Housing and Home Finance Agency.","parent_excerpt":"When we move beyond the provision of individually fitted prosthetic appliances for disabled veterans into the field of compensation, the sound and equitable method of meeting the needs of disabled veterans is through the provision of a carefully considered scale of compensation rates paid in cash on a monthly basis.","explanation":"Each redirects the legitimate need away from a selective benefit and toward an established, generally applicable administrative program characterized as more sound and equitable."},{"child_excerpt":"The Veterans' Administration direct loan program was established for the purpose of granting to veterans for whom guaranteed loans were not readily available an equal opportunity... The terms and conditions of these direct loans were intended to conform as closely as possible to the guaranteed loans.","parent_excerpt":"The original program of automobiles for disabled veterans was intended to provide timely rehabilitative assistance... Under S. 2115, the factor of mobility would be largely disregarded... S. 2115 would abandon the principle upon which the original program was based.","explanation":"Both reconstruct the original limiting principle of a veterans' program and argue that the proposed expansion departs from that principle."}]}
